A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SONICS dataset and SpecTTTra research. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures and appendices are readable, and retained material can be matched across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v3 reports original detection experiments, a human evaluation and efficiency measurements in Section 4 and Tables 2, 4–6, alongside dataset analyses in the appendices.

after.justification: v4 retains those original results and additionally reports token ablations, external-generator evaluations, specialized detector comparisons and dataset-quality checks.

M1.justification: The dataset-generation pipeline, spectral and temporal tokenizers, positional embeddings, Transformer encoder, pooling, classifier and three SpecTTTra variants remain unchanged. The tokenizer pseudocode and training objective also match. New component-removal experiments are ablations, not revisions to the proposed method.

E1.justification: v4 adds evaluation on 394 SkyMusic and 36 SeedMusic songs from external generator families (Appendix D.1, Table 8). This substantially extends generalization coverage beyond the existing Suno/Udio generator variants. The original SONICS and SingFake coverage is retained.

E2.justification: v4 newly evaluates AASIST, ResNet + Spec., ResNet + LFCC and Wav2Vec2 + AASIST against SpecTTTra in Table 9, with additional external-generator results in Table 8. These specialized comparators were not evaluated in v3; the original ConvNeXt, ViT and EfficientViT comparisons remain.

E3.justification: New evaluation designs include temporal-only and spectral-only controls, varying spectral clip size while holding temporal clip size fixed, external-generator testing with randomly initialized controls, and manual vocal/style audits using 50 samples each. Section 6 also describes inspecting the 50 closest synthetic/real song matches. Existing splits, training budgets and benchmark settings are retained rather than demonstrably revised.

E4.justification: v4 adds component ablations in Section 4.4, external-generator robustness tests in Appendix D.1, genre-distribution analysis, vocal/style quality audits, a similarity-based copying check and analyses of correct and incorrect classifications in Appendix E. These address architectural contributions, dataset validity and failure modes beyond v3's existing duration, embedding and style analyses.

E5.justification: Both versions report averaging 100 inference-timing runs after five warm-up runs. Neither provides training-seed counts, confidence intervals, performance error bars or significance tests. The new randomly initialized controls do not introduce seed or repeated-run uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: The original numerical entries in Tables 2–6 are unchanged. New Table 7 reports 120-second F1 scores of 0.91 for temporal-only tokens, 0.92 for spectral-only tokens and 0.97 for their combination. Table 8 adds external-generator results, including SpecTTTra-γ scores of 0.80 on SeedMusic and 0.60 on SkyMusic at 120 seconds. Table 9 adds detector results and failures, including AASIST's 0.91 F1 at five seconds and out-of-memory failure at 120 seconds.

T1.justification: The token-count expressions and tokenizer equations, Equations 1–3, retain the same mathematical content. Neither version contains additional theorems or proofs, and the new empirical ablations do not revise the formal model.

C1.justification: The central dataset, architecture, long-context and benchmarking contributions, including headline performance and efficiency gains, are retained. However, v4 removes the introduction's blanket assurance that synthetic songs are free from copyright issues; its ethics statement instead acknowledges copyright concerns and specifies noncommercial licensing, qualifying an important dataset-use claim.

C2.justification: v4 introduces interpretations of token complementarity, external-generator performance declines, possible overfitting and audible classification failures. It also discusses English-only applicability, gender imbalance and copyright concerns. Appendix A newly argues that genre shortcuts are absent, although the distribution plot alone does not establish this. The original limitations paragraph is retained in Appendix G rather than removed.

D1.justification: v3 promises a future resource release; v4 states that code and data are available and that supplementary materials contain source code and configurations. It additionally specifies CC BY-NC 4.0 licensing, distribution of real songs through YouTube links, and manual collection of external-generator samples. Existing hyperparameters, hardware, generation costs, pseudocode and prompt templates are retained.

R1.justification: The largely retained related-work section is substantially supplemented by Appendix F's direct positioning against specialized song detectors and Appendix D.1's connection to cross-generator media-forensics research. New references also contextualize imperceptible artifacts and generated-dataset practices. This expands the substantive research positioning beyond citation-format changes.

P1.justification: Most existing method, experiment and prompt prose is retained, with limited abstract and contribution-list editing. Dataset costs and limitations move to appendices, acknowledgments are removed, and new section headings and an appendix contents page organize the additions. The revision does not extensively rewrite the retained scientific narrative.

P2.justification: The document changes from a two-column layout to a single-column ICLR format, extensively repositioning and resizing retained displays. v4 adds the genre-distribution figure and Tables 7–9, adds total hours to Table 1, and expands benchmark captions and unseen-generator annotations. Existing figures and prompt tables are retained despite relocation and renumbering.

improvement.justification: v4 addresses important validation gaps in v3 through component ablations, specialized detector comparisons and external-generator tests that expose generalization failures (Tables 7–9). Dataset-quality audits further strengthen the dataset contribution without changing the original headline results. Some reporting remains problematic: Table 7's short-audio token counts conflict with the stated dimensions, and genre-robustness and broad superiority interpretations overreach their evidence. Nevertheless, the added controlled comparisons and failure evidence substantially improve the paper's empirical foundation.
